summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She later held a post at the University of Washington, where she taught Qian Lin.

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953). He worked at Deccan College (~1953–1956), Utrecht University (1959–1961), and the University of Chicago from 1961.
J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Colombo from ~1967 to 2002 and at SOAS University of London from ~1996 to 1997.

J. Gordon Melton (born 1942) works in religious studies. He studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1968) and held posts at UCSB (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).

J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He subsequently held an academic appointment at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1923, where he taught Surendranath Dasgupta.

J. Robert Oppenheimer (1904–1967) studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and learned Sanskrit under Arthur William Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley and Caltech (~1929–1947), directed the Manhattan Project (~1942–1945), and headed the Institute for Advanced Study (~1947–1966).

J. Thomas Rimer (born 1933) is a Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Princeton University (1954) and Columbia University (1968, 1971). He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis, UCLA, the University of Maryland (~1986–1991), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1991–2013).

Jack Copeland (born 1950) is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1975–1979). He held positions at the University of Portsmouth and the University of Canterbury, joining the latter in 1985.

Jack Goody (1919–2015) worked in history and archaeology. Educated at St Albans School and St John's College, Cambridge (~1938–1946), he later held a post as a professor at the University of Cambridge from ~1973 to 1984.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999. He subsequently held an academic appointment at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Grimm (1785–1863) was a linguist who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1805). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and at Frederick William University Berlin beginning in 1841.
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2013.

Jacob N. Kinnard (born 1968) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held positions as Assistant Professor of Religion at William & Mary and as a faculty member at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob P. Dalton (born 1969) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1996–2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held posts at Yale (2005), SOAS (~2005–2008), and UC Berkeley (~2008).

Jacob Samuel Speyer (1849–1913) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (~1867–1872). He held posts at Amsterdam (1877–1889), Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel (1853–1938) was a Swiss linguist and Indologist who studied at Basel, Göttingen (under Theodor Benfey), Leipzig, and Oxford. He served on the faculty at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and held a chair at Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone (born 1949) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her BA at SFSU and her MA and PhD at UCLA under William R. LaFleur, later teaching at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Julius Lipner (attested 2005). She held an academic post at the University of Manchester, attested in 2005.

Jacques André (1910–1994) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris until 1948, he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), EPHE (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1919, the University of Paris, and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).
